title: Colts hold off Dolphins, but questions about coach, QB cloud Indy’s future
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — The Indianapolis Colts are in a strange position 10 weeks into the NFL season. Any win is likely too late to help their faint playoff hopes. Any loss doesn’t improve their draft positioning, at least not in the first round, as they traded their top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft to the New York Jets last season for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

So what did Sunday’s 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium mean for the Colts (3-7), who  snapped a five-game losing streak? For the immediate future, not much — unless it’s the beginning of a winning run that helps coach Shane Steichen’s case for keeping his job for 2027.

The offense, which repeatedly drew boos from the home crowd, struggled – hurt especially by 13 penalties. What movement the Colts did get came on the ground, with running backs Jonathan Taylor (16 carries for 83 yards) and Seth McGowan (12 carries for 77 yards and a touchdown) doing most of the damage. Indy’s defense helped the effort by scoring a touchdown early in the third quarter after Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered a fumble in the end zone.

Meanwhile, the rebuilding Dolphins dropped to 1-8, losing the first start of Kyle McCord’s NFL career. The 2025 sixth-round pick, starting in place of the injured Malik Willis, completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards. He also rushed for a touchdown.

Kicking issues cost Miami. Zane Gonzalez missed 47- and 51-yard field goals, as well as an extra point.

The loss keeps the Dolphins in the hunt for the No. 1 overall pick in the draft as one of three teams with one win or less. The Tennessee Titans dropped to 1-8 on Sunday, while the winless Los Angeles Chargers play on Monday night.

The Dolphins head to Buffalo next week to take on the AFC East-leading Buffalo Bills. The Colts play Thursday night at Houston.

If the Colts were going to fire Steichen midseason, the perfect opportunity appeared to be after a 42-7 loss at Jacksonville in Week 8. They chose not to make a move, and now it seems that he’ll make it through the end of the season. Beyond that, however, feels like a stretch even if the Colts stack some wins. The bottom line is that if the Colts fail to make the playoffs, which still seems likely, Steichen will have had four years at the helm with no postseason appearances. Although Steichen is under contract through the 2028 season, it’s hard to justify keeping any coach with such little overall success.

Taylor’s touches have dwindled considerably in recent weeks, and I don’t blame anyone for speculating whether that had to do with Taylor’s name being in many rumors at last week’s trade deadline. Now that he’s staying, it appears the Colts are trying to keep him fresh, which seems like a sound approach given McGowan’s ascension. Taylor, who eclipsed 10,000 career scrimmage yards Sunday, has the second-most carries in the NFL since he was drafted in 2020, trailing only Baltimore’s Derrick Henry. He was still plenty effective against the Dolphins as he piled up 103 yards from scrimmage, but it doesn’t hurt to have a viable counterpunch in McGowan, whose 77 rushing yards were a career high.
